title: Settlement Desk Guidance: One Open Settlement Agreement per Placed Account
content:
# Settlement Agreements — One Open Settlement per Placed Account

**Rule.** Under Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements a consumer may hold settlements on any number of placed accounts, but each settlement covers exactly one placed account. A new offer is extended only when no other settlement on the same placed account is offered or accepted; a consumer who wants different terms on an open offer has the open offer withdrawn with the reason superseded by new offer before the new one is extended, and an accepted settlement is never replaced while it is in good standing.

## Basis of the rule

- **No limit per consumer.** There is no cap on how many settlements one consumer holds across their accounts; the limit is one open settlement per placed account.
- **What counts as open.** A settlement on the same placed account in status offered or accepted stands in the way of a new offer on that account.
- **Evidence.** The test is made on Ridgeline's own settlement records for the placed account the new offer would cover, as they stand before the offer is extended — the account the settlement is on and its status — not on the consumer's description of earlier offers.

## Judgement table for the same placed account

| Existing settlement on the same placed account | New offer under this rule |
|---|---|
| None | not barred by this rule |
| One in status offered, and the consumer wants different terms | extended only after that open offer is withdrawn with the reason superseded by new offer |
| One in status offered, and the consumer does not ask for different terms | not extended |
| One in status accepted, in good standing | not extended; an accepted settlement in good standing is never replaced |
| Only settlements in status expired, withdrawn, defaulted or fulfilled | not barred by this rule |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A hypothetical consumer owes three placed accounts and holds an accepted settlement on one of them. An offer on either of the other two accounts is not barred by this rule, because each settlement covers its own account.
2. On a hypothetical account with an open offer, the consumer asks for a different schedule. The open offer is withdrawn with the reason superseded by new offer, and only then is the new offer extended on that account.
